_about: How each custom mechanic maps onto Forge. tier: script = a Forge card script can express it today; engine = needs new Java code in a Forge fork (fits Forge's structure); manual = no engine can enforce it, a person resolves it. 'question' = the wording needs the author's ruling before anyone can implement it.

mithridatism.how: Your poison-loss limit is 30 instead of 10 for the whole game if this card is your commander. Needs a small change to Forge's poison check.
mithridatism.ruling: Always on when the card is your commander from the start of the game, wherever it is (battlefield or command zone).

eminent mithridatism.how: You can't lose from poison counters. Same change as Mithridatism.

indulge curiosity.how: Each player in turn order, starting with the caster, chooses whether to participate; 'participant' means the players who joined. Forge can ask each player; the bots need logic for when joining is worth it.
indulge curiosity.ruling: A whole-table card: every player, the caster included, chooses whether to participate, in turn order (unless the card says otherwise), seeing earlier choices.

capture.how: Aura-style static: enchanted creature can't attack or block.

transcendence.how: The [bracketed] text applies only while you have fewer than 20 poison counters. Needs a condition on part of a card's text.
transcendence.ruling: The [bracketed] text is off only while you have 20 or more poison counters; below 20 it's back.

majestic veil of elegance.how: While attacking: indestructible, can't be blocked by creatures with flying.

mesmerize.how: Opponents can't attack you until you attack or this leaves the battlefield; meanwhile you can't draw cards or gain life. Needs a per-game flag for 'you attacked'.
mesmerize.ruling: Lasts until this card leaves the battlefield or until you attack. While it lasts you can't draw cards or gain life (reminder text updated).

military.how: Opponents can't gain control of it; whenever a creature an opponent controls dies, put a +1/+1 counter on it (Forge script).
military.ruling: Any opponent's creature that dies while this is on the battlefield gives it a +1/+1 counter. Opponents can't take control of it by any means, spells or abilities.

plane.how: Your reminder says it's void until a full set exists. Ignored by the engine until defined.

poison.how: Cast trigger: you get N poison counters (also when cast from other zones).

herbal properties.how: Herbal cards live in a bag outside the deck. Maomao's, Surei's and Xiaomao's 'draw from Maomao's Bag' puts a random bag card into your hand; you may cast one herbal card per turn for free, then it returns to the bag and your turn ends. Needs the bag zone in Forge.
herbal properties.ruling: Free to cast. One herbal card per turn. They come from Maomao's Bag: Maomao, The Apothecary, Surei, The Scheming and Xiaomao draw from it, a random card. After it's used it goes back to the bag and your turn ends.

influence.how: Can't be the target of abilities from creatures (Forge script).
influence.ruling: Can't be targeted by creature abilities; 'destroy all' effects still work (reminder text updated).

secretive movement.how: Cast face down with its own power and toughness, never turned face up; 'reveal' is replaced by discarding a card (revealed only when you can't). Needs engine code.
secretive movement.ruling: Always cast face down, keeping its own power and toughness, and it can't be turned face up. If something would reveal it, you discard a card from your hand instead; only if you can't is it revealed. It's never revealed to an opponent otherwise (you can look at it).

herbal specialist.how: Trigger: one or more permanents you control to graveyard → Food or Treasure.

misfortune.how: Trigger on damage to you: draw a card, lose 1 life.

endowment.how: As you cast it, choose an opponent; they create the matching hairpin token (the [bracketed] text). Like Bloomburrow's gift; needs the token linked to its card.
endowment.ruling: The hairpin tokens should be tokens (count 0), not cards in the deck.

legacy of the garnet pavilion.how: Anthem: other Nobles you control get +1/+1.

fragile.how: State trigger: a player was dealt more than 10 damage this turn → destroy this.

stasis.how: Turns off 'end your turn' on Herbal Properties. Depends on the herbal bag work.

insecurity.how: ETB trigger on Noble/Soldier: -2/-0, then may transform if power ≤ 0.

infatuated.how: During its controller's next turn the creature's activated abilities can't be activated and its triggered abilities don't trigger. Needs code to switch off one creature's triggers.
infatuated.ruling: For the creature's controller's next turn.

obsession.how: Replacement: a Shogi Piece that would be destroyed/exiled goes face down under this card; returns to hand when it leaves.

conquer.how: Static with a count condition (6+ Shogi Pieces).

eternity.how: Cast trigger: search for a named card, put it onto the battlefield or into your hand.

desire.how: Until end of turn, whenever you get poison counters, add that much mana in any combination of {B} and {G} (Forge script).
desire.ruling: The mana empties between steps, like normal mana.

command.how: Gain control until end of turn + haste, lifelink, connive. 'Only once per creature' needs per-game memory of chosen creatures.

absolute command.how: Gain control for as long as it lives; 'once per creature' again needs per-game memory.

frontline ace.how: Like Master Warcraft: you choose which creatures attack and block (Forge supports that).
frontline ace.question: “Designate all attackers and blockers” — including how your opponents' creatures block?

stealth.how: Can't be the target of abilities from creatures.

superior cloak.how: Discard a card: phase this out until end of turn.

blaze luminous.how: Enters with a shield counter; {3}: put a shield counter on it, sorcery speed.
blaze luminous.question: Can it have more than one shield counter?

stark hadron cannon.how: 28 damage that destroys even indestructible permanents — damage ignoring indestructible needs code.
stark hadron cannon.question: If the target is indestructible, is it destroyed anyway, or just takes the damage?

jousting lance.how: Attack trigger, condition 'blocked by a commander'.

cockpit ejection system.how: {T}: return this to its owner's hand.
cockpit ejection system.question: “Sacrifice this creature, you may return this creature to its owner's hand” — once sacrificed it's in the graveyard. Do you mean return it from the graveyard, or bounce it instead of sacrificing?

pilot.how: Alternative to Crew: tap the named creature to crew. Forge's Crew only counts power.

bloodlust.how: Trigger: when it kills a creature, put N loyalty counters on it.
bloodlust.question: Bloodlust is used on Luciano Bradley, a creature with no loyalty. Should he be a planeswalker?

re-engineer.how: Choose keywords from a list; they replace the creature's keywords.

code bearer.how: Part of the Geass/Code system: can't be destroyed or exiled except by Code users while you control your commander.

code user.question: “Only a Fully Awakened Code user can kill a Code bearer to inherit its skills” — how is the kill done (combat damage? any effect?), and what exactly is inherited?

reckless.how: Attack trigger: discard any number of nonland cards, that many +1/+1 counters.

burn.how: Damage that never wears off and can't reduce toughness below 1 is a new kind of damage.
burn.question: Damage to a creature normally heals at end of turn — does Burn damage stay? “Its caster's power” — the power of the creature with Burn?

eternal.question: “Can only be killed in one instance of damage” — damage from separate sources in one turn doesn't add up? So it only dies to a single hit ≥ its toughness?

fully awakened.how: Part of the Geass/Code system (Evolve level ≥ 3).

evolve.how: Part of the Geass/Code system: Evolve level counter, +1 per Geass ability used, max 3.

timeless.how: Enters with N timeless counters; upkeep: remove one, then if none, may transform (like Saga/Vanishing).

immortality.how: Undying is script; 'immune to deathtouch' needs code.

charm.how: Can't attack you or your planeswalkers until the end of its controller's next turn.
charm.question: Used both as a keyword on creatures (C.C.) and as a verb (“Charm target creature/player”). What does it mean on C.C. herself, and what does charming a player do?

nirvana.how: You can't lose and opponents can't win (like Platinum Angel).

paramount.how: Can't attack or block; upkeep: V.V. The Outer God gets -N/-N.
paramount.question: Permanent -N/-N or until end of turn? Does it stack each upkeep?

primitive.how: Can't attack or block; upkeep: V.V. The Outer God gets +N/+N.
primitive.question: Same as Paramount: permanent or until end of turn?

code.how: New card type that grants its abilities to a creature. Part of the Geass/Code system.

geass.how: Geass counters plus abilities labelled “Geass Ability” that interact with Evolve, Code and Lelouch's draw trigger.

rampage.how: Triple P/T; must attack a random player each turn or be sacrificed. Random attack target needs code.
rampage.question: Clashes with the real keyword Rampage N. Rename?

full-house.how: The [bracketed] text is void until the full set is created (your reminder), so the engine leaves it out; the rest of the card plays normally.

patterns.regex: hasn[’']t been chosen this game|once per creature|only once per card
patterns.label: per-game memory

Maomao, The Apothecary.note: “Draw a card from Maomao's Bag”: a random herbal card into your hand (Herbal Properties ruling).

Surei, The Scheming.note: Draws from Maomao's Bag like Maomao (ruling).
Surei, The Scheming.question: The text says “Return Suirei from your graveyard” but the card is named Surei — same card?

Xiaomao.note: Draws from Maomao's Bag like Maomao (ruling).

Red-Handed.note: Players may lie and call “Red-handed”: a social game no engine can referee. Simulations skip it; in live play it's resolved by hand.

Curses and Criticizing [Art 2].note: “Without negotiation, once everyone decided” — hidden simultaneous choices; possible in software but bots can't judge it meaningfully. Resolve by hand at first.

Lakan Fight.question: “Deal -X/-X to target creature” — do you mean “target creature gets -X/-X until end of turn”?

Euphemia li Britannia.question: “Reduce X damage divided between target permanents” — prevent the next X damage, divided as you choose, this turn?

Euphie Special.question: “Negate all damage received” — prevent all damage that would be dealt to creatures you control this turn?

Sayoko Shinozaki.question: “Negate any damage received by Nunnally” — prevent all damage dealt to Nunnally, always?

Withered Blue Rose.question: “Roll a D6, then randomly choose an effect” — is the effect the number rolled, or a second random pick?

Temple of Heaven.question: “Whenever a player adds {G} … add another {G}” — like Mana Reflection for green only, for every player?

Locked Chest.note: “The second time” means every second search or shuffle: the 2nd, 4th, 6th… (ruling).

Mordred.question: “Use Hadron Cannons instead when attacking … if target blocked creature …” — instead of dealing combat damage? And “Amalgamate all four Hadron Cannons” — does it need the other three Hadron cards?

Lancelot Albion.question: Power is “7-5” and “attacks normally” / “use Hadron cannons” — what are its power and the exact attack trigger?

Guren Mk II.question: “Guren's attack is doubled against flying creature” — double damage to flying creatures it fights or is blocked by?

Shinkirō, Zero’s Ace.question: “Whenever Shinkirō is a non-creature artifact … add {5} to target player's commander cost as long as it's active” — while it isn't crewed? And “Absolute Defense System” isn't defined anywhere.

Zero Requiem Finale.question: “Exile Lelouch vi Britannia” — the commander (Master of Geass) or the other Lelouch card? “Total power counters you control” — the counters on The Power of Absolute Obedience?

Ragnarök Connection.note: Taking ownership of every exiled card changes who owns cards — large change, keep for later.

Lelouch’s Gambit.note: Controlling another player's turn is Mindslaver — Forge supports it.

Devious Plotting.note: “Entered the battlefield more than twice” counts the whole game, through zone changes (ruling). Needs per-card history.

Never Ever Say-.question: Meld: does “-That Name Again.” need to be on the battlefield, or can it be in your hand? “Becomes all card types” — creature too (with what P/T)?

Jinshi, Imperial Moon.question: “{4B}: Jinshi, Imperial Moon.” has no effect — what does it do?

Ashford Academy.question: Text ends at “Whenever you connive, add” and it's a Saga with no chapters. What's the full card?

Geass Mausoleum.question: Typed Island Swamp but taps for {W} or {B}, and mentions Godless Shrine. Which is right?

Charles zi Britannia, Immortal Emperor.question: Has loyalty abilities but is a creature with no loyalty. Planeswalker with what loyalty? “Elite” isn't a Magic supertype.

Luciano Bradley, Knight of Ten.question: “2:” — is that “+2:”? Creature with loyalty abilities: planeswalker?

Luciano Bradley, Vampire of Britannia.question: Creature with loyalty abilities and Bloodlust: planeswalker with what loyalty?

Ash Phoenix, Nameless Flame.question: “Deal X Burn damage equal to its power to any blocking creatures” and “Apply Burn” — see the Burn questions.

Rumors of House Verdigris.question: “Reset the commander cost of all players” — remove all commander tax? “If a ‘Win the game’ effect is used by an opponent, negate that effect” — like Platinum Angel's opponent half?

Silver in Cash.question: The spell becomes a basic land card permanently (in every zone, for the rest of the game)?

Lady Fuyou.note: Counters every spell that targets her, your own included (ruling).

rulings.compact-costs: Shorthand like {TBG} or {3BG} in a cost means {T}, {B}{G} / {3}{B}{G}: tap plus that mana (author's ruling).
